Subject: RFP: Encryption + key custody clarifications

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the quick onboarding earlier this week. We attached the encryption section of our RFP as a separate PDF (see attachment) — we need written confirmation on a number of operational controls before we include Redwood in the shortlist:

- Do you support customer-supplied keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed import/export protection?
- What import protocols do you support (KMIP, PKCS#11, Azure Key Vault wrap, etc.)?
- How does rotation work for keys that back long-lived cached model state (KV cache)?
- Do you offer mTLS between our VPC and your private deployment control plane?
- Evidence of key provenance, audit trails, and tamper logs (we will request for procurement).

Can we get a concise technical playbook and a short list of supported HSM vendors/certifications? Procurement would like a formal reply by end of week to slot us into the RFP review.

Attachment: Tekvia_RFP_Encryption_Appendix.pdf (1.2MB, PDF)

Thanks,

- Rotation: configurable rotation windows; KV cache invalidation patterns supported to avoid stale wrapping keys.

On Wed, Nov 18, 2026 at 10:03 AM -08:00 Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Maria —
>
> Appreciate the clear list. We can absolutely provide the details you need. I attached our KMS orchestration playbook (high level) and looped in Rishi (applied ML/inference security) and Priya (product security) to answer the technical specifics and point to operational evidence.

Thanks Sean / Maria — below is a technical appendix addressing each of Maria’s bullets. I kept items concise; happy to expand any section with diagrams or sample configs.

1) BYOK and HSM-backed import/export
- Modes supported: a) Import into Redwood-managed HSM (customer-provided key material wrapped by an HSM-wrapped KEK), b) External KMS federation where customer keeps root key and we hold ephemeral wrapped keys (no unwrapped root key ever stored).
- Import protocols: KMIP (stateless key import), PKCS#11 for on-prem HSM connectors, and a secure wrap/unwrap REST API for cloud key wraps (AES-GCM wrapping + RSA-OAEP for asymmetric scenarios).
- HSM certs: we integrate with vendors supporting FIPS 140-2 Level 2/3 and common FIPS-validated modules; we can share vendor matrix per NDA.

2) Key rotation and KV cache implications
- Rotation model: keys have a primary and versioned previous keys. Rotation is automated via policies (time-based or manual).
- KV cache: for model KV caches that rely on envelope keys, we offer atomic rotation: new envelope keys are provisioned, cache entries are rewrapped lazily on read or proactively via background rewrap jobs. For latency-sensitive paths we provide a dual-key window where both old and new wrapping keys are accepted for a configurable overlap.
- Rollback & roll-forward: audit-safe operations include non-destructive key versions and the ability to mark a key as deprecated before deletion; complete deletion requires authorized multi-party approval.

3) TLS details and mutual auth
- Protocols: TLS 1.2 (recommended minimum) and TLS 1.3 supported.
- Cipher suites: AEAD suites only (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305). We can provide exact cipher list if you require a compliance mapping.
- mTLS: available for Redwood Private deployments and for Dedicated peering; we support client cert provisioning and rotation via our control plane API.

4) Key provenance, audit logs, and evidence
- Audit logs: immutable event streams for key lifecycle events (create/import/rotate/disable/destroy), signed and timestamped, with HSM-backed attestations when applicable.
- Exports: we can provide redacted audit exports and a sample HSM attestation bundle. For procurement we’ll include a checklist of artifacts (HSM attestations, KMS configuration snapshot, rotation policy history, and example audit lines).

5) Operational controls & separation of duties
- Access controls: RBAC + scoped API keys for key managers, with MFA for admin actions.
- Escrow & recovery: multi-party signing required to export key material from a sealed escrow. We support time-locked escrow for emergency key recovery with full audit.

Limitations / notes:
- Our hosted API (shared tenancy) supports BYOK federation but does not allow unwrapped persistent storage of customer root keys; persistent unwrapped root key storage is only available in Private deployments under a signed support arrangement.
- HSM vendor support matrix will be provided under NDA; common vendors we support today include Thales, Utimaco, and AWS Nitro (CloudHSM).

Attachments referenced: redwood-kms-playbook-v1.2.docx (detailed playbook), sample-audit-export.csv (redacted) — I will upload evidence links to the drive listed below.

If you’d like visuals, I can put together a 30‑60 slide deployment diagram showing federation vs import paths.

—Rishi Malhotra
Principal, Applied ML Security
Redwood Inference
